text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Spokesman for Nigeria's ruling council, Major-General John Inienger, says 1997 fiscal budget will be "common man's budget" and that council holding final meeting on Tuesday to approve it.
- Domestic airline operators divided on whether or not the government should totally deregulate air fares.
- Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi heads to Liberia on Tuesday to assess progress in implementing peace plan in that country.
- World Meteorological Organisation signs agreement with Nigeria to cite its sub-regional headquarters in Abuja.
- State oil firm NNPC scraps 30-day credit facility for oil marketing firms, who must now pay before they get supplies of petroleum products.
- Nigeria Airways plans to start flights to Dubai, United Arab Emirates, within next month.
- Unemployment is highest in southwestern Nigeria, the opposition's stronghold, according to an official survey.
- Shortage of funds is threatening government's ambitious housing programme, says housing minister Major-General Abdulkareem Adisa.
- The issue of releasing political detainees will be on the agenda when the ruling council reconvenes in Abuja on Tuesday to consider this year's fiscal budget, sources say.
- Police retire two top officers and several others in major shake-up of police force that involves posting of senior officers to different commands around the country.
- Nigerian stock exchange maintains upbeat track with turnover up by 89.86 percent on Monday over last Friday.
